title: Ticket
purpose: Follow one ticket: read the conversation with the laboratory, see where it stands, reply, or raise a follow-up once it is closed.
summary: One of your tickets: where it stands, the conversation with the laboratory, and a box to reply. A closed ticket takes a follow-up ticket instead.

tasks.title: Reply to the laboratory
steps: Write your message in [[Your reply]] under Reply.
Select [[Send reply]]. Your message joins the Conversation.

tasks.title: Answer a ticket that waits for you
steps: Read the notice Waiting for you and the latest message in the Conversation.
Send the information with [[Send reply]]. The ticket goes back to the laboratory.

tasks.title: Continue a closed ticket
steps: Select [[New follow-up ticket]], fill in the form and send it.

tasks.title: Ask for the same thing again
steps: Check the copied answers, fill what is blank and select [[Send ticket]].

good_to_know: Replying to a ticket that is Waiting for you or Resolved sends it back to the laboratory, and it shows With the laboratory again.
A closed ticket takes no more replies. If it closes while you write, your text comes back unsent; select [[New follow-up ticket]] to send it there.
Laboratory replies are signed with the team's name and the laboratory's name, never a person's.
You never see the laboratory's internal notes, who is assigned, priorities, service clocks, complaint records or patient links.
If the ticket changed after you opened the page, your reply is not sent. Copy it and open the ticket again from [[Tickets]]; if it already shows there, it was sent: do not send it again.

items.label: Status
items.description: Where the ticket stands, in your wording: With the laboratory, Waiting for you, With a third party, Resolved or Closed. The header also shows the ticket number, the topic and the site.

items.label: Waiting for you
items.description: A notice that the laboratory is waiting for information from you. Replying sends the ticket back to the laboratory.

items.label: Resolved
items.description: A notice that the laboratory has resolved the ticket. If something is still wrong, reply and it goes back to the laboratory.

items.label: Closed
items.description: A notice that the ticket takes no more replies, with a link to open a follow-up ticket that records this ticket's number.

items.label: New follow-up ticket
items.description: Shown only on a closed ticket. Opens the ticket form with this ticket's number carried along.

sections.title: Ticket facts
paragraphs: The first panel is titled with the ticket's subject.

items.label: Ticket
items.description: The ticket number. The Tickets breadcrumb returns to the same search, status, sort and page when you open a ticket from the list.

items.label: Topic
items.description: What the ticket is about, in the laboratory's client wording.

items.label: Site
items.description: The site the ticket is about, or Not about one site.

items.label: Your reference
items.description: The reference you gave when raising the ticket, or None given.

items.label: Raised, Last update
items.description: When the ticket was raised and when it last changed.

items.label: Follow-up of, Followed up in
items.description: Follow-up of links to the closed ticket this one follows up. Followed up in lists up to three follow-up tickets raised from this one. Both show only tickets your account can see.

sections.title: Form details
paragraphs: Shown when the ticket was raised with one of the laboratory's ticket forms. It lists the form's name and the answers you gave, under the labels they had then, and answers the laboratory records for you, such as a tracking number. Fields only the laboratory uses are not shown.

items.label: Request again
items.description: Opens the same form with your answers copied, so you can check them and send a new ticket. Only answers shown to you on this ticket are copied. Dates, times, confirmations, patient details and order or sample numbers are left blank. Shown while the laboratory still offers the form to you.

sections.title: References
paragraphs: This panel appears only when the laboratory chose to show you references to records in its other systems for this ticket. Person-level links are never shown.

items.label: Reference, Type, System
items.description: The reference's label, what kind of record it is and the system it belongs to.

sections.title: Conversation
paragraphs: The messages between you and the laboratory and the changes of status, oldest first. Nothing else about the ticket appears here.

items.label: You wrote
items.description: A message sent by your own account.

items.label: Message from your organization
items.description: A message sent by another portal account at your organization, with Sent by and their name.

items.label: Reply from the laboratory
items.description: A reply from the laboratory, signed with the team's name and the laboratory's name.

items.label: Files on a message
items.description: Files sent with a message are listed under it with their size and Not scanned. Select a name to download the file; it is never opened in the portal. Files the laboratory keeps internal, or has withdrawn, are not shown. Not scanned means no virus scanner has checked the file. Its type was checked from its content (an image must decode, every page or frame of it, a PDF must have a document structure, a Word or Excel file must be a valid package without macros), and it is always downloaded rather than opened here, but it can still carry harmful content. Open it only with up-to-date software, and ask the sender when something looks wrong.

items.label: Status: ...
items.description: A change of status, in your wording, with its time.

items.label: No messages yet
items.description: The empty state when nothing has been said yet.

sections.title: Reply
paragraphs: The Reply panel is shown while the ticket is With the laboratory, Waiting for you, With a third party or Resolved. It is not shown on a closed ticket.

Reply not sent takes its place when the laboratory closed the ticket after you opened the page, before your reply reached it (also while it was being saved): nothing is sent, files included, and the text you wrote is shown read only, under Your reply, not sent, with a New follow-up ticket button. A reply of files only gets the notice alone. Copy the text into the follow-up ticket and choose the files again there. If the reply already shows in the Conversation, it was sent earlier (a page sent again after a lost connection, for example): do not send it again.

items.label: Your reply
items.description: Required. Seen by the laboratory. Do not enter patient names or dates of birth.

items.label: Files
items.description: Optional. Photos, scans and documents for the laboratory: PDF, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF, text, CSV, Word (.docx) or Excel (.xlsx), up to 5 files and 10 MB together. On a phone you can take a photo or pick one from your library. Each file is checked, and an image may have at most 100 pages or frames. After a validation error, Files lists the previous selection. Choose the files again, or check the box to leave out the ones you omit. Files are not scanned for viruses.

items.label: Send reply
items.description: Sends the message and returns to the Conversation with the message Reply sent to the laboratory. A reply on a ticket that was Waiting for you or Resolved sends it back to the laboratory, so its status becomes With the laboratory. A ticket closed after you opened the page refuses the reply and shows Reply not sent with your text.

items.label: Ticket changed meanwhile
items.description: The page shows the ticket as it stood at the moment you opened it: the conversation, status, details and references are read together, and the reply box sends against that moment. If the ticket changed after you opened the page, the reply is refused with a message saying so, and the text you wrote stays in the box. Sending it again from this page, or reloading it, is refused the same way (also when your own earlier reply was what changed the ticket, so the page never sends it twice): copy the text and open the ticket again from Tickets. If your reply already shows in the Conversation, it was sent: do not send it again. Otherwise paste it and send it. Choose files again if you had chosen any.

items.label: Your reply, not sent
items.description: Shown under Reply not sent: the text of a reply the closed ticket refused, read only so you can select and copy it. It is not stored: opening the ticket again no longer shows it. Reloading this response sends the refused reply again, which is refused the same way and shows the text again.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Only an active client portal account can open this page, and only for a ticket it may see: one it raised, or one of its organization's or its sites' tickets when the laboratory gave it that access. A ticket in a restricted category is seen only by the account that raised it. Any other ticket number answers as not found. The page never shows internal notes, logged contacts, who is assigned, priorities, service clocks, complaint records or patient links. Sending a reply is a POST-only action of this page and has no page of its own. Your account is checked again as the page is read: an account deactivated, or moved to another organization, while the page opens is refused.
